title: Cell cycle arrest of S. cerevisiae in conjunction with labeling of the cell wall
protocol: Wash the cells twice in ice-cold PBS and then resuspend them in 0.5 mM sodium m-periodate in PBS (freshly prepared).
Incubate for 15 min on ice.
Wash the cells 2× with ice-cold PBS.
Incubate on ice for 30 min with 0.5 mg/mL Texas Red--hydrazide or 13 mM CF488A Aminooxy in PBS (diluted from 100× stocks).
Wash the cells twice and return them to growth medium ± methionine.
Label the cells in growth medium by adding a 1/100 volume of rhodamine-Concanavalin A stock (1 mg/mL).
Incubate for 15 min ice.
After two washes in growth medium ± methionine, resuspend the cells in medium ± methionine.
Grow shaking cultures of cells in synthetic medium lacking methionine.
When they reach mid-log phase (OD600 = 0.5–1), sediment samples in Eppendorf tubes and resuspend in an equal volume of complete synthetic medium ([methionine] = 20 mg/liter).
Shake for 3 h at 23°C.
Sediment cell cultures.
Apply 0.5–1.0 μL samples of the pellet to the surface of agarose pads after exposure of the agarose by sliding off the upper slide.
Overlay with a No. 1 thickness coverslip.
For imaging in excess of 15 min duration, trim the agar to the dimensions of the coverslip and seal with vaseline to reduce drying.
Examine samples in a Deltavision RT epifluorescence microscope with an automated stage using an oil immersion objective.
Capture z-stacks at intervals of 0.2–0.5 μm.
Set the exposure time to 0.05–1 s and field size to 1040 × 1040 pixels, binning 1 × 1.
Collect through-focal series spanning a total of 6 μm.
Remove out-of-focus light using the Softworks deconvolution program.
If imaging living cells is inconvenient, add formaldehyde to cultures to achieve a final concentration of 3.7%.
Agitate cultures with added formaldehyde for 5 minutes.
Wash cultures once with growth medium to quench free aldehydes.
Store samples in water at 4°C for 1–2 days before examination.
